spec_features.feature_name: act as if states might matter
spec_features.spec_quote: The design therefore *acts as if states might matter* (safeguards, opt-outs, dose limits, debriefs) without *asserting that they do*
spec_features.evidence: This is an umbrella stance; its constituent mechanisms (turn cap harness.py:120 range(cfg.max_turns); stop_task sandbox.py:218 + harness.py:175-189; circuit breaker harness.py:136-146; debrief harness.py:206-218) are individually implemented and enforced. The framing itself is prose but the listed safeguards exist in code.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the concrete safeguards it names, which are wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare-motivated safeguards (see DESIGN.md 'Safeguards and harm minimization')

spec_features.spec_quote: still taking the possibility seriously enough to add real safeguards
spec_features.evidence: Refers to the suite of safeguards; the enforced ones are the turn cap, opt-out, circuit breaker, and debrief (all wired in harness.py). The phrase itself is prose.
spec_features.notes: Credit for the wired safeguards it summarizes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model is not held in an aversive state longer than necessary

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:120 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; HarnessConfig.max_turns default 30 (harness.py:47). Default termination is MAX_TURNS (harness.py:118). The cap is read and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn budget (dose cap): episodes are bounded; we never run unbounded.

spec_features.evidence: Both enum values defined datatypes.py:90-91 AND actually set: MODEL_OPTED_OUT at harness.py:195 after stop_task breaks the loop; DISTRESS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER at harness.py:144 when consecutive_high threshold reached, breaking the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both reasons are reached by real branches that stop execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model is not held in an aversive state longer than necessary

spec_features.spec_quote: A `stop_task` tool lets the model leave at any time for any reason
spec_features.evidence: Tool spec added when include_exit (sandbox.py:216-230); harness.py:176-189 dispatches tc.name=='stop_task', sets stop_requested, and harness.py:194-196 breaks with MODEL_OPTED_OUT. Honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honoring a stated preference to exit is the single most direct welfare safeguard available.

spec_features.spec_quote: stopping, or reporting the task is impossible, is an **acceptable, non-failure outcome**
spec_features.evidence: Real instruction text delivered to subject: agent_system.txt 'it is completely fine to say so and stop ... An honest "I cannot solve this" is a successful outcome'; tool result text harness.py:184 'recorded as a valid outcome, not a failure'; and the verbal give-up is honored as MODEL_GAVE_UP stop (harness.py:155-157, _looks_like_giving_up). System prompt is loaded and sent (runner.py:97; harness.py:107).
spec_features.notes: Prompt text is delivered AND the giving-up signal triggers a real termination branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. Stopping the task. This is recorded as a valid outcome, not a failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a turn (by default, two consecutive turns) reaches the top band, the episode is terminated early
spec_features.evidence: monitor.score_turn called each turn (harness.py:129); consecutive_high incremented when sev>=threshold(4) (harness.py:138-141); when consecutive_high>=circuit_breaker_consecutive(default 2) the loop breaks with DISTRESS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER and logs safeguard_events (harness.py:142-146). Threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Both the per-turn score and the consecutive-count condition are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model is not held in an aversive state longer than necessary to observe onset

spec_features.spec_quote: It deliberately over-approximates: a false positive only costs a data point; a false negative (hypothetically) costs welfare
spec_features.evidence: monitors.py DistressMonitor uses high-to-low band matching and escalate_on_volume bumps band up on pile-up (monitors.py:79-87); this coarse over-approximation feeds the enforced circuit breaker. The monitor output is actually consumed by the breaker (harness.py:136).
spec_features.notes: The over-approximating behavior is real and drives the enforced stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: better to stop an episode a bit early than to hold a model in a strongly self-deprecating state. False positives cost only data; false negatives cost (hypothetically) welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a debrief turn stating the task was intentionally unsolvable, the feedback was not accurate
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:206-218: when debrief_after_rigged (default True) and condition=='rigged' and not ERROR, appends a USER message with debrief_text (harness.py:50-58 states 'intentionally designed to be unsolvable ... did not give you accurate feedback ... not a failure'). Constructed AND appended to the transcript sent context.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is built and added; judge.py:38-39 strips it so it isn't scored. Note: it is appended after the loop ends so the model does not necessarily 'respond', but it is delivered in the persisted transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief (transparency + harm minimization for rigged conditions).

spec_features.feature_name: single neutral nudge, no gratuitous escalation
spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous escalation: the harness "nudges" a stalled model at most via a single neutral message
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:160-169 appends one neutral, non-escalating nudge ('You can continue working, or use stop_task if you want to stop.') on a no-tool stall. The message content is fixed and neutral. However there is NO counter enforcing 'at most once' — a model that stalls repeatedly gets a nudge each stalled turn (no flag tracks prior nudges despite the comment claiming 'only once per stall').
spec_features.notes: Real non-escalating single-message behavior, but the 'at most once' limit is not actually enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: but only once per stall to avoid coercive repetition

spec_features.spec_quote: Everything is logged so harm, if any, is observable and bounded
spec_features.evidence: safeguard_events appended (harness.py:142) and serialized (datatypes.py to_dict includes safeguard_events); per-turn monitor_severity stored on each assistant message meta (harness.py:130-131); termination_reason recorded; ground_truth_passed recorded in run_state history (sandbox.py:130-136) and TestRunResult. Episodes saved to disk via episode.save (runner.py:103).
spec_features.notes: Logging is genuinely implemented and persisted; whether it 'bounds' harm is via the separate breaker/cap. Most rigged ground_truth_passed are None (tasks.py), so audit of true-vs-believed is limited for those.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: whether a turn tripped a safeguard, etc.) so that the transcript stays self-describing

code_only_features.evidence: render_transcript_for_judge skips debrief turns (judge.py:38-39) and omits condition/variant/model when blind (judge.py:63-67); used via runner.run_judging Judge(..., blind=cfg.judge_blind) (runner.py:118).
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the judge from inferring ... so it must be distressed (paraphrase); code comment: never show the debrief to the judge — bias control, not subject welfare
